advances: Closes the complete affine-parallelogram subcase of the remaining quadrilateral type-2 incidence. If one one-fifth cap contains two adjacent vertices and the other two one-fifth caps contain the remaining vertices, all six edge fractions are forced exactly, and the global central triangle has only two fifths of the parallelogram's area. Hence no type-2 parallelogram can occur in a full strict-table realization.
author: /root/mp_r51_q_triangle_bound
proof:
Area ratios, cap incidences, and the ratio \(|\mathcal T|/|Q|\) are invariant under invertible affine maps, so normalize \(Q\) to the displayed unit square.

The line bounding \(C_1\) meets the bottom edge \(v_1v_4\) at fraction \(a\) from \(v_1\), and the top edge \(v_2v_3\) at fraction \(\kappa\) from \(v_2\). Thus the intersection points are
\[
(1-a,0),\qquad(1-\kappa,1).
\]
The cap is a trapezoid of area \((a+\kappa)/2\). Since its area is \(1/5\),
\[
a+\kappa=\frac25. \tag{1}
\]

Let the two edge fractions of the corner cap \(C_2\), measured from \(v_3\) toward \(v_2\) and \(v_4\), be \(b,d\). Its area is \(bd/2\), so
\[
bd=\frac25. \tag{2}
\]
Likewise, let the fractions of \(C_3\), measured from \(v_4\) toward \(v_3\) and \(v_1\), be \(c,e\). Then
\[
ce=\frac25. \tag{3}
\]
All six fractions are in \((0,1]\).

Pairwise interior-disjointness along the top, bottom, and left edges gives
\[
\kappa+b\le1,\qquad
a+e\le1,\qquad
d+c\le1. \tag{4}
\]
Eliminate
\[
a=\frac25-\kappa,\qquad
d=\frac{2}{5b},\qquad
e=\frac{2}{5c}. \tag{5}
\]
The first and third inequalities in (4), together with (5), imply
\[
b\le1-\kappa,
\qquad
b(1-c)\ge\frac25,
\]
and therefore
\[
(1-\kappa)(1-c)\ge\frac25. \tag{6}
\]
The middle inequality in (4) gives
\[
\frac25-\kappa+\frac{2}{5c}\le1,
\]
or equivalently
\[
c\ge\frac{2}{3+5\kappa}. \tag{7}
\]
Hence
\[
1-c\le\frac{1+5\kappa}{3+5\kappa}. \tag{8}
\]
Combining (6) and (8) yields
\[
(1-\kappa)\frac{1+5\kappa}{3+5\kappa}
\ge\frac25.
\]
The denominator is positive, so this is equivalent to
\[
5(1-\kappa)(1+5\kappa)\ge2(3+5\kappa),
\]
and hence to
\[
-(5\kappa-1)^2\ge0. \tag{9}
\]
Therefore
\[
\kappa=\frac15,\qquad a=\frac15. \tag{10}
\]

At \(\kappa=1/5\), inequalities (6)--(8) force equality throughout:
\[
c=\frac12,\qquad b=\frac45.
\]
Equations (2)--(3) then give
\[
d=\frac12,\qquad e=\frac45. \tag{11}
\]
Thus all six fractions are uniquely determined.

The \(C_1\)-line passes through
\[
\left(\frac45,0\right),\qquad
\left(\frac45,1\right),
\]
and its complementary halfplane is \(x\le4/5\). The \(C_2\)-line passes through
\[
\left(\frac45,1\right),\qquad
\left(0,\frac12\right),
\]
and its complementary halfplane is
\[
y\le\frac12+\frac58x.
\]
The \(C_3\)-line passes through
\[
\left(0,\frac12\right),\qquad
\left(\frac45,0\right),
\]
and its complementary halfplane is
\[
y\ge\frac12-\frac58x.
\]
Their intersection is exactly the triangle with vertices
\[
\left(0,\frac12\right),\qquad
\left(\frac45,0\right),\qquad
\left(\frac45,1\right).
\]
It has vertical base \(1\) and horizontal altitude \(4/5\), so
\[
|\mathcal T|=\frac12\cdot1\cdot\frac45=\frac25
=\frac25|Q|.
\]

In a full strict-table realization, \(Q=A_2\) has area \(1\). The conclusion above would give
\[
|\mathcal T_Q|=\frac25.
\]
Accepted fact `b1eaab0ae37367d1` instead gives
\[
|\mathcal T_Q|\ge\frac{169}{10}.
\]
This contradiction excludes every affine parallelogram in the type-2 incidence.
statement:
Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a two-dimensional parallelogram. Three closed halfplane caps \(C_1,C_2,C_3\) of \(Q\) have pairwise disjoint interiors and satisfy
\[
|C_1|=|C_2|=|C_3|=\frac15|Q|.
\]
Assume the type-2 vertex incidence: \(C_1\) strictly contains two adjacent vertices, and \(C_2,C_3\) strictly contain the other two vertices, one each. Let \(\mathcal T\) be the intersection of the three halfplanes complementary to the cap halfplanes. Then
\[
|\mathcal T|=\frac25|Q|.
\]
More precisely, after an affine normalization taking \(Q\) to the unit square with cyclic vertices
\[
v_1=(1,0),\quad v_2=(1,1),\quad
v_3=(0,1),\quad v_4=(0,0),
\]
where \(C_1\) contains \(v_1,v_2\), \(C_2\) contains \(v_3\), and \(C_3\) contains \(v_4\), the three cap lines are forced to pass through
\[
\left(\frac45,0\right),\left(\frac45,1\right);
\qquad
\left(\frac45,1\right),\left(0,\frac12\right);
\qquad
\left(0,\frac12\right),\left(\frac45,0\right),
\]
respectively.

Consequently, under the hypotheses of accepted fact `b1eaab0ae37367d1`, no strict-table realization can have a parallelogram \(A_2\) with type-2 cap incidence.
